title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Manufacturing Engineering (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Manufacturing Engineering (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following CNC G-code functions 'Verify Metric Coordinate Positions'?
questions.explanation: G21 is the G-code command for setting metric units in CNC programming.

questions.questionText: What is a measure of the degree of plastic deformation that has been sustained at fracture?
questions.explanation: Ductility measures how much plastic deformation a material can undergo before fracture.

questions.questionText: The major advantage of process layout over product layout is
questions.explanation: Process layout offers more flexibility as it groups similar processes together.

questions.questionText: Which of the following measures may be taken to extend fatigue life?
options: Improving the surface finish by polishing
Introducing surface residual compressive stresses by shot peening
questions.explanation: Shot peening introduces beneficial compressive residual stresses on the surface, which helps prevent fatigue crack initiation and propagation. The other options (polishing, eliminating discontinuities, reducing mean stress) also extend fatigue life, but shot peening is particularly effective for fatigue resistance.

questions.questionText: The permanent magnetic and ferroelectric behaviors of some ceramic materials are due to:
questions.explanation: These properties arise from specific arrangements of atoms in the crystal structure.

questions.questionText: A type of production system which is characterized by dedicated production of large quantities of one product or limited model variations of it is:
questions.explanation: Mass production focuses on high-volume output of standardized products.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not considered as the important assumption of the simple theory of bending?
options: The beam is initially straight and unstressed
Plane cross-sections remain plane before and after bending
There will be resultant force perpendicular to any cross-section
The elastic limit is nowhere exceeded
questions.explanation: In the simple theory of bending, it is assumed that there is no resultant force perpendicular to any cross-section. The resultant of the normal stresses on any cross-section consists only of a moment, with no net force perpendicular to the section.

questions.questionText: If a cylindrical bar is subjected to a direct pull along its axis then it is said to be:
questions.explanation: Axial pulling creates tensile stress in the bar.

questions.questionText: What is a measure of the deformation of the material that is non-dimensional?
questions.explanation: Strain is the dimensionless measure of deformation. It is defined as the change in length divided by the original length, making it a ratio with no units.

questions.questionText: In dealing with work in relation to energy transfer of a thermodynamic system, which one is wrong?
options: Work is done by the system when it is used to turn a turbine and thereby generate electricity in a turbine-generator
natural value for work indicates that work is done by the system on its surroundings
negative value indicates that work is done on the system by its surroundings
Work is done on the system when a pump is used to move the working fluid from one location to another
questions.explanation: In thermodynamics, a positive value for work indicates that work is done by the system on its surroundings, not a 'natural' value. The term 'natural value' is incorrect terminology.

questions.questionText: Identify what lubricants cannot function when applied to an operating machine
questions.explanation: Lubricants reduce friction but don't directly reduce applied force.

questions.questionText: The Carnot cycle, regardless of what the working substance may be, always has the same basic processes. Which one is the correct one among these processes:
options: reversible isothermal process in which the temperature of the working fluid decreases from the high temperature to the low temperature
reversible adiabatic process in which heat is transferred to or from the high temperature reservoir
reversible adiabatic process in which heat is transferred to or from the low temperature reservoir
reversible isothermal process in which heat is transferred to or from the low temperature reservoir
questions.explanation: Carnot cycle includes isothermal heat rejection at low temperature.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a reason why equipment damage can be caused by failure?
questions.explanation: Availability is a result of reliability and maintenance, not a cause of damage. Equipment damage can be caused by failures in design, manufacturing defects, or improper maintenance, but availability itself is an outcome, not a cause.

questions.questionText: Which is wrong about cutting fluids?
options: Cutting fluid provides lubrication between the chip and the tool
The effects of lubricant vary with cutting conditions and work materials
Will increase tool life and improved surface finish
Will reduce both coefficient of friction and the shear angle
questions.explanation: Cutting fluids reduce the coefficient of friction but increase the shear angle, not reduce it. A larger shear angle is beneficial as it reduces cutting forces and improves chip formation.

questions.questionText: What is a special type of four-high rolling mill in which each of the two smaller working rolls are backed up by two or more of the larger back-up rolls?
questions.explanation: Cluster mills have multiple backup rolls supporting each work roll. This configuration provides additional support and allows for rolling of harder materials or achieving higher reductions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not under the category of natural ceramics?
questions.explanation: Porcelain is a manufactured ceramic material.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following cannot be taken as a factor for the quality of the product in the metal casting process?
options: differences in the physical properties and constitution of the alloys
chemical activity and solubility for gases
the type of energy used to melt the material
questions.explanation: The type of energy used to melt the material (whether electric, gas, induction, etc.) doesn't directly affect casting quality as long as proper temperature control and melting practices are maintained. The other factors significantly influence casting quality through microstructure, defect formation, and physical properties.

questions.questionText: What is a typical resistance welding process used to join overlapping sheets by local fusion?
questions.explanation: Spot welding is commonly used for joining overlapping sheets. It uses electrical resistance to generate heat at the contact point, creating a localized fusion weld.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following mechanism will not be appropriate for shaping and slotting machines?
questions.explanation: Scotch-yoke isn't typically used in shaping machines.

questions.questionText: What can be defined as the capacity of a material to undergo deformation under compression without rupture?
questions.explanation: Forgeability describes compressive deformation capacity. It is the ability of a material to be shaped by forging operations, which involve compressive forces that deform the material without causing fracture.

questions.questionText: What is the basic principal raw material for all ferrous metals, which is obtained by smelting iron ore, coke and limestone in the blast furnace?
questions.explanation: Pig iron is the direct product of blast furnace smelting. It is the crude iron that serves as the starting material for producing steel and other ferrous alloys.

questions.questionText: What is used for forming large circular moulds of symmetric kind by revolving a sweep attached to a spindle?
questions.explanation: Sweep patterns create circular shapes by rotation. A sweep pattern consists of a profile that is rotated around an axis to generate the mold cavity, making it efficient for creating large symmetrical circular castings.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cannot be considered as cutting parameters of milling and turning operations
questions.explanation: Tool orientation is setup, not a cutting parameter.

questions.questionText: What process is used to create threads on cylindrical parts by rolling them between two dies?
questions.explanation: Thread rolling is the cold forming process for making threads. It uses hardened dies to plastically deform the material, creating threads without removing material, resulting in stronger threads with better surface finish.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is considered as a thermal cutting Process?
questions.explanation: Arc cutting is a thermal cutting process that uses the heat from an electric arc to melt and separate metal. Gas cutting and plasma cutting are also thermal processes, but abrasive cutting is mechanical.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong about grease and grease lubrication
options: The single most distinguishing property of grease is its viscosity
Drop point is one characteristic of grease
Greases are a mixture of lubricating oil and usually a soap base
questions.explanation: Grease is distinguished by its consistency, not viscosity.

questions.questionText: The ability or probability of an item, under stated conditions of use, to be retained in, or restored to, a state in which it can perform its required functions, when maintenance is performed under stated conditions and using prescribed procedures and resources is:
questions.explanation: Maintainability refers to ease of maintenance and restoration.

questions.questionText: Which type of energy is not appropriate to remove excess material in the modern or non-traditional manufacturing processes?
questions.explanation: Bio energy isn't used in non-traditional machining processes.

questions.questionText: What is a measure of the degree of disorder within a system?
questions.explanation: Entropy quantifies disorder in a system. It is a thermodynamic property that measures the number of ways energy can be distributed in a system.

questions.questionText: What uses computers to aid the development of part programs to drive machine tools?
questions.explanation: CAM (Computer Aided Manufacturing) focuses on generating machine tool programs. It translates design data into instructions that control CNC machines and other automated manufacturing equipment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about ultrasonic machining?
options: able to effectively machine all materials whether they are electrically conductive or insulator
the machining tool must be selected to be highly wear resistant
it is basically used to machine very big/large workpieces
versatile machining process as far as properties of materials are concerned
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic machining is typically for small, intricate work.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is incorrect about network scheduling techniques for a project?
options: Critical Path Method (CPM) is extensively used as dynamic control tools in the management of a large project
An activity which does not consume any kind of resource is Dummy Activity
The time calculated along the critical path is the project completion time
Backward Pass Computations is employed to calculate the earliest finish time of activities
questions.explanation: Backward pass calculates latest times, not earliest.

questions.questionText: Cutting parameter that cannot directly be considered to determine the rate of metal removal in metal turning process is:
questions.explanation: Rake angle affects tool life but not directly metal removal rate.

questions.questionText: In the design of any structural element or component, the design engineer expected to consider:
questions.explanation: Factor of safety is fundamental in design considerations.

questions.questionText: Which material is not appropriate to cut using abrasive jet machining?
questions.explanation: Wood is typically not processed with abrasive jet machining.

questions.questionText: A 25 mm diameter bar is subjected to an axial tensile load of 100 kN. Under the action of this load a 200mm gauge length is found to extend 0.19×10^-3 mm. Determine the modulus of elasticity for the bar material.
A 240 cm pipe is in series with a 120 cm pipe. The speed of the water in the 240 cm pipe is 2 m/s. What is the water speed in the 120 cm pipe?
questions.explanation: Using the continuity equation (A₁V₁ = A₂V₂), when the pipe diameter is halved, the area is reduced to 1/4 (area = πr²). To maintain the same flow rate, velocity must increase by a factor of 4. So, 2 m/s × 4 = 8 m/s.

questions.questionText: In ______ operation, work material is cut by a shearing action between the adjacent sharp edges of the punch and the die.
questions.explanation: Blanking and piercing involve shearing action.

questions.questionText: The pressure at which the liquid phase and the vapor phase of a material will be in thermal equilibrium is: Vapor pressure is also called saturation pressure, and the corresponding temperature is called saturation temperature.
questions.explanation: Vapor pressure defines equilibrium between phases.

questions.questionText: In a press tool process, which factor will result in premature wear of the tools and a risk of tool breakage?
questions.explanation: Insufficient clearance increases tool wear and breakage risk.

questions.questionText: What makes scheduling in cellular manufacturing more difficult than the traditional one?
options: Use of group tooling significantly increases setup time
Machines are more flexible in performing various operations
High demands and low variety of products
questions.explanation: Machine flexibility adds complexity to scheduling.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not recommended inert gases for using in TIG welding?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is not recommended as a shielding gas for TIG welding because it is highly reactive and can cause hydrogen embrittlement in many metals, especially steel. Argon, helium, and their mixtures are inert gases commonly used for TIG welding shielding.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not true in case of bending of a beam cross-section?
options: the upper surface of the beam is subjected to tension
the bottom surface of the beam is subjected to compression
the stress in the neutral axis became maximum
questions.explanation: In beam bending, the stress at the neutral axis is zero, not maximum. The stress increases linearly from zero at the neutral axis to maximum values at the extreme fibers (outer surfaces).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not considered as a common casting defect?
questions.explanation: Corrosion occurs after casting, not as a casting defect.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the principal variation of gating position?
questions.explanation: Top-front gating isn't a standard classification.

questions.questionText: Which is true about the purpose of parting sand?
options: used to keep the green sand not to stick to the pattern
used to back up the facing sand
used to stick the cope and drag
questions.explanation: Parting sand prevents sticking to patterns.

questions.questionText: What is a process used to fabricate both clay and nonclay compositions, including electronic and magnetic ceramics as well as some refractory brick products?
questions.explanation: Slip casting is versatile for various ceramic compositions. It involves pouring a ceramic slurry (slip) into a porous mold, where water is absorbed, leaving a solid ceramic layer that can be removed and fired.

questions.questionText: In the process planning activity, select the correct sequence of process planning steps among the choices provided below.
options: Selection of processes and tools; sequencing the operations; grouping of operations; selection of inspection instruments
Sequencing the operations; selection of processes and tools; grouping of operations; selection of inspection instruments
Selection of inspection instruments; selection of processes and tools; sequencing the operations; grouping of operations
Grouping of operations; selection of processes and tools; sequencing the operations; selection of inspection instruments
questions.explanation: Standard sequence is process/tool selection → operation sequencing → grouping → inspection planning.

questions.questionText: What is a process for joining two similar or dissimilar metals by fusion?
questions.explanation: Welding involves fusion of base metals. The metals are melted and fused together, often with a filler material, creating a strong metallurgical bond.

questions.questionText: What is a machine used for filling and uniform ramming of molding sand in molds?
questions.explanation: Jolt machines provide uniform sand packing. They use a jolting action to compact the sand uniformly around the pattern, ensuring consistent mold density.

questions.questionText: Among the different rolling defects ______ are usually the result of poor material ductility at the rolling temperature.
questions.explanation: Cracks result from insufficient ductility during rolling.

questions.questionText: On the basis of stress-strain behavior, polymers fall within the following general classifications except:
questions.explanation: Polystyrene is a specific polymer, not a behavior classification.

questions.questionText: What is a mechanical material removal process or an abrasive process used to erode holes or cavities on hard or brittle workpieces by using shaped tools?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic machining uses abrasive slurry for hard materials. A vibrating tool drives abrasive particles against the workpiece, removing material through micro-chipping, making it ideal for hard, brittle materials like ceramics and glass.

questions.questionText: In which types of steel category, the stainless steel is included
questions.explanation: Stainless steels are low-carbon with alloying elements.

questions.questionText: Materials are often placed in service at elevated temperatures and exposed to static mechanical stresses such as in high-pressure steam lines cases. The type of deformation under such circumstances is:
questions.explanation: Creep is time-dependent deformation under stress at high temps.

questions.questionText: What is a method of holding the material while the punch is withdrawn on the upward stroke during a blanking or piercing operation?
questions.explanation: Stripping is the process of removing the workpiece or scrap from the punch during the upward stroke in blanking or piercing operations. Stripper plates or springs are used to prevent the workpiece from being lifted with the punch.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about composite materials?
options: The reinforcement materials can be in the form of particles, fibers and fabrics
There will be a homogeneous distribution of constitutes
The matrix materials can be metals, polymers and ceramics
Have better mechanical properties than metals and alloys
questions.explanation: Composites are inherently heterogeneous materials.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of transformer in the Arc welding process?
options: to step up the usual supply voltage (200 - 400 volts) to the normal open circuit welding voltage (500-900 volts)
to step down the usual supply voltage (200 - 400 volts) to the normal open circuit welding voltage (50-90 volts)
to step up the supply voltage (500 - 900 volts) to the normal open circuit welding voltage (200-400 volts)
to step up the usual supply voltage (200 - 400 volts) to the normal open circuit welding voltage (300-900 volts)
questions.explanation: Welding transformers reduce voltage to safer levels.

questions.questionText: What is used to produce seats in the form of extra recesses for core placement in the mould?
questions.explanation: Core prints create seats for cores in molds. They are projections on the pattern that form recesses in the mold where cores can be positioned and supported during casting.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the commonly used material for spot welding electrodes?
questions.explanation: Copper tungsten combines conductivity with wear resistance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not considered as the basic property of molding sand and core sand?
questions.explanation: Roundness isn't a fundamental molding sand property.

questions.questionText: The type of metal cutting tools which may be produced from tungsten, titanium and cobalt. The tools also contain high degree of hardness and resistance able to retain hardness at elevated temperatures up to 1000°C is:
questions.explanation: Carbide tools maintain hardness at high temperatures.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the possible modes (or methods) of failure of engineering components?
options: Elastic yielding - force and/or temperature induced
questions.explanation: Elastic yielding is not a failure mode because elastic deformation is fully reversible; the component returns to its original shape when the load is removed. The other options represent actual failure mechanisms where permanent damage occurs.

questions.questionText: What is used to receive molten metal from the melting furnace and pour it into the mold cavity?
questions.explanation: Ladles are used to transfer molten metal from furnaces to molds. They are typically made of steel with a refractory lining to withstand high temperatures and are designed for safe handling and pouring of molten metal.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not considered as the basic process of chemical machining?
questions.explanation: Chemical forging isn't a standard chemical machining process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a principal property of tool steels?
questions.explanation: Cutting resistance isn't a standard tool steel property.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about water jet machining?
options: Thick parts can be easily cut
There is no heat generated in water jet cutting
limited number of materials can be cut economically
Does not produce any dust or particles that are harmful
questions.explanation: Water jet cutting can process a wide variety of materials economically, including metals, plastics, composites, glass, ceramics, stone, and more. This versatility is one of its main advantages.

questions.questionText: For ______ materials, internal stress concentrations arise within the material due to the presence of, flaws, impurities or graphite flakes.
questions.explanation: Brittle materials are sensitive to stress concentrations.

questions.questionText: What is the arrangement of links in a chain fashion which permits relative motion between the links?
questions.explanation: Kinematic chain describes linked moving components. It is an assembly of rigid bodies (links) connected by joints that allow relative motion, forming the fundamental building block of mechanisms and machines.

questions.questionText: Blowholes are large holes in the weld caused by:
options: Gas being trapped, due to moisture
questions.explanation: Blowholes result from trapped gases during welding.

questions.questionText: The energy stored by a fluid mass may not appears in the form of:
questions.explanation: Hydraulic energy isn't a fundamental energy storage form.

questions.questionText: Which one is not the basic component of a numerical control system:
questions.explanation: Product design exists before NC programming.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about Semiconductors
options: They have electrical properties that are intermediate between the electrical conductors and insulators
Atoms in semiconductors are arranged in a very orderly manner
They have very large molecular structures, often chain-like in nature
questions.explanation: Semiconductors have intermediate conductivity properties.

questions.questionText: Which is not true about the general sources of natural molding sands?
options: the beds of sea, rivers, lakes
questions.explanation: Power plant byproducts aren't natural sand sources.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not under the Oxy-Fuel Gas Welding Processes?
questions.explanation: Argon isn't used in oxy-fuel welding processes.

questions.questionText: A close-coiled helical spring, constructed from wire of 10 mm diameter and with a mean coil diameter of 50mm, is used to join two shafts which transmit 1 kilowatt of power at 4000rev/min. If the number of turns of the spring is 10 and the modulus of elasticity of the spring material is 210 GN/m2, what will be the maximum stress set up in the spring material?
questions.explanation: Torque T = Power/Angular velocity = 1000W/(4000rpm×2π/60) = 2.39Nm. Maximum shear stress τ = 16T/(πd³) = 16×2.39/(π×0.01³) = 48.6MN/m². Note that for torsional applications, the shear modulus G would be used rather than Young's modulus E, but the question indicates a value of 210 GN/m², which is typical for E.

questions.questionText: How much will be the number of instantaneous center for a Whitworth mechanism of having 6 numbers of links?
questions.explanation: Number of ICs = n(n-1)/2 = 6×5/2 = 15 for 6 links.

questions.questionText: What is the pressure at the bottom of a 7.5m-tall storage tank of gasoline fluid at 25°C. Assume that the fluid is with atmospheric pressure 101 kPa on the top surface? (take g = 9.8m/s2, ρ_gasoline= 750 kg/m3)
questions.explanation: Pressure at depth = P_atm + ρgh = 101 kPa + (750 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² × 7.5 m)/1000 = 101 kPa + 55.125 kPa = 156.125 kPa ≈ 156.2 kPa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about Specific enthalpy (h) of a substance
options: Unlike temperature and pressure, it is a property of a substance
It is defined as h=u+Pv (u= specific internal energy, P= pressure and v= specific volume)
specific enthalpy is given using reference of pressure and temperature
questions.explanation: Specific enthalpy is defined as h = u + Pv.

questions.questionText: Air that has a mass density of 2.5 kg/m³ flows in a pipe with a diameter of 30 cm at a mass rate of flow of 5 kg/s. What is the mean velocity?
questions.explanation: Mean velocity = mass flow rate / (density × cross-sectional area) = 5 kg/s / (2.5 kg/m³ × π × (0.15 m)²) = 5 / (2.5 × π × 0.0225) = 5 / 0.17671... ≈ 28.31 m/s.

questions.questionText: Of the following, identify the none-ferrous metallic alloy
questions.explanation: Brass is a copper-zinc alloy (non-ferrous).

questions.questionText: The recrystallization temperature of ______ metals is always below the room temperature.
questions.explanation: Lead and tin recrystallize at room temperature.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about soft soldering?
options: It is used not only to make a mechanical bond but also to provide a leak proof seal
Soft solders are alloys of tin and lead
Solder melts at a temperature above 500 °C
It will also be used to provide a permanent electrical connection
questions.explanation: Soft solders are primarily tin-lead alloys.

questions.questionText: A part which used to support or hold in position long cores to produce hollow section in casting is called___
questions.explanation: Chaplets support cores in casting molds.

questions.questionText: What is the impact of impurities on the mechanical properties of a metal alloy?
options: Impurities always weaken the material, regardless of type
All impurities improve ductility but reduce tensile strength
Impurities has no effect on mechanical properties
Certain impurities can enhance strength through solid solution strengthening, while other can lead to brittleness
questions.explanation: The impact of impurities on metal alloys depends on the specific type and concentration. Some impurities can strengthen the material through solid solution strengthening (where impurity atoms create lattice strain that impedes dislocation motion), while others may segregate at grain boundaries and cause embrittlement. For example, carbon in iron creates steel with enhanced strength, while sulfur in steel can cause hot shortness (brittleness at high temperatures).

questions.questionText: What is the main role of grain boundaries in materials?
options: Serve as barriers to dislocation motion
questions.explanation: Grain boundaries are interfaces between crystals (grains) in polycrystalline materials. Their primary role is to act as barriers to dislocation motion, which is fundamental to strengthening mechanisms in materials (Hall-Petch strengthening). When dislocations encounter grain boundaries, they cannot easily cross due to the crystallographic misorientation, requiring more stress for continued deformation, thus strengthening the material.

questions.questionText: What type of property is ductility?
questions.explanation: Ductility is a mechanical property that describes a material's ability to deform under tensile stress before fracture. It is typically measured as percent elongation or reduction in area during a tensile test. Mechanical properties include strength, hardness, ductility, toughness, and elasticity, all of which describe how materials respond to applied forces.

questions.questionText: If a material shows increased ductility at higher temperature, what can you infer about its microstructure?
options: It is likely to be amorphous
It has a low melting point
questions.explanation: Increased ductility at higher temperatures indicates that the grains become more mobile. At elevated temperatures, thermal energy activates additional slip systems and enables grain boundary sliding, dislocation climb, and other thermally activated deformation mechanisms. This increased mobility allows for greater plastic deformation before fracture, which is why many metals are hot-worked above their recrystallization temperature.

questions.questionText: Vacancy defects in solids is a sub type of
questions.explanation: Vacancy defects are classified as point imperfections (or point defects) in crystalline materials. Point imperfections are zero-dimensional defects that occur at or around a single lattice point. They include vacancies (missing atoms), interstitials (extra atoms in between lattice sites), and substitutional atoms (foreign atoms replacing host atoms). Line imperfections include dislocations, while volume imperfections include voids and inclusions.

questions.questionText: How do you evaluate the toughness of a new material?
questions.explanation: Toughness is evaluated through impact tests such as the Charpy or Izod impact test. Toughness represents a material's ability to absorb energy before fracture, combining both strength and ductility. While tensile tests can provide information to calculate toughness (area under stress-strain curve), impact tests are specifically designed to measure energy absorption under dynamic loading conditions, making them the standard method for evaluating toughness.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a common method for processing ceramics?
questions.explanation: Casting is not a common method for processing traditional ceramics. Ceramics typically have high melting points and are processed through powder metallurgy techniques. Common ceramic processing methods include: sintering (heating powder compacts below melting point), injection molding (for complex shapes with binder), and extrusion (for bricks, pipes, and tiles). Casting is more common for metals and some specialized ceramic slurries (slip casting), but not a general ceramic processing method.

questions.questionText: What is the primary advantage of using polymers in manufacturing?
questions.explanation: The primary advantage of polymers in manufacturing is their lightweight nature combined with excellent corrosion resistance. Polymers typically have densities much lower than metals (0.9-2.0 g/cm³ vs 2.7-8.0 g/cm³ for metals) and are inherently resistant to many corrosive environments. While they generally have lower thermal conductivity, lower melting points, and lower strength compared to metals, their weight savings and corrosion resistance make them ideal for many applications.

questions.questionText: Which polymer processing technique involves heating and forcing material through a die?
questions.explanation: Extrusion is the polymer processing technique where material is heated and forced through a die to create continuous profiles. The process involves feeding plastic material into a heated barrel, where it is melted and then forced by a screw through a shaped die. This produces continuous lengths of products like pipes, sheets, films, and profiles. Blow molding uses air pressure, thermoforming uses heated sheets over molds, and compression molding uses pressure in a closed mold.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors does NOT significantly affect the mechanical properties of composite?
questions.explanation: The color of a composite does NOT significantly affect its mechanical properties. Color is an aesthetic or optical property that can be modified with pigments or dyes without changing the fundamental mechanical behavior. In contrast, fiber orientation determines anisotropy and directional strength, matrix material determines load transfer and environmental resistance, and environmental conditions (temperature, moisture) can significantly affect mechanical performance through degradation or property changes.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of sintering in ceramics processing?
options: To densify and strengthen the material
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of sintering is to densify and strengthen the ceramic material. Sintering involves heating a compacted powder to a temperature below its melting point, causing atomic diffusion that bonds particles together, reduces porosity, and increases density. This process transforms the weak, porous powder compact into a strong, dense solid with improved mechanical properties. Shaping occurs before sintering (green forming), while densification and strengthening are the main objectives of the sintering step.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a common application of composite materials?
questions.explanation: Everyday paper products are NOT typically considered composite materials in the engineering sense, though technically paper is a cellulose fiber composite. In engineering contexts, composites refer to engineered combinations of distinct materials (like fiberglass, carbon fiber composites) designed for specific properties. Common composite applications include: aerospace components (lightweight, high-strength parts), electrical insulators (fiberglass-reinforced polymers), and building materials (fiber-ceboard, reinforced concrete).

questions.questionText: In a face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure, each atom is in direct contact with how many nearest neighbors?
questions.explanation: In a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, each atom has 12 nearest neighbors, giving it a coordination number of 12. The FCC structure has atoms at each corner and at the center of each face of the cube. Each corner atom is shared by 8 adjacent unit cells and touches the face-centered atoms. This close-packed arrangement (74% packing efficiency) provides many slip systems, making FCC metals like aluminum, copper, and nickel highly ductile.

questions.questionText:
Rank the magnitude of the diffusion coefficients from greatest to least for the following four systems:

1. N in Fe at 700°C

2. Cr in Fe at 700°C

3. N in Fe at 900°C

4. Cr in Fe at 900°C

Note: both Fe and Cr have a Body centered cubic crystal structure and atomic radii for Fe, Cr, and N are 0.124, 0.125, and 0.065 nm
questions.explanation:
The correct ranking is 3 -- 1 -- 4 -- 2 (N in Fe at 900°C > N in Fe at 700°C > Cr in Fe at 900°C > Cr in Fe at 700°C).
Diffusion coefficient depends on:
1. Temperature: Higher temperature increases diffusion (Arrhenius behavior)
2. Atomic size: Smaller atoms (N: 0.065 nm) diffuse faster than larger atoms (Cr: 0.125 nm) in the same matrix
3. Interstitial vs substitutional: N diffuses interstitially (much faster), while Cr diffuses substitutionally (slower)
Thus, N diffuses faster than Cr, and 900°C gives faster diffusion than 700°C for both.

questions.questionText: The type of bond at which when the atoms of one element give up their electron(s), which are in turn attracted to the atoms of some other element to increase their electron count in the outermost shell to eight?
questions.explanation: This describes ionic bonding. In ionic bonding, one atom (typically a metal) donates electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration, becoming a positively charged cation. Another atom (typically a nonmetal) accepts these electrons to complete its octet, becoming a negatively charged anion. The electrostatic attraction between these oppositely charged ions forms the ionic bond. Classic examples include NaCl (sodium donates electron to chlorine) and MgO.

questions.questionText: Which of the following crystal structures has the highest atomic packing density?
questions.explanation: Both Hexagonal Close-Packed (HCP) and Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) have the same atomic packing factor of 0.74 (74%), which is the highest possible for equal-sized spheres. However, if we must choose one, both are equally dense. The question's options include both, but typically HCP and FCC are considered equally close-packed. BCC has 0.68 (68%), and Simple Cubic has 0.52 (52%) packing efficiency. Since both HCP and FCC are equally close-packed, and HCP is listed first, it's the correct choice.
